meta.title: AnyCompany Web Application on AWS: Three-Tier Architecture in a VPC
meta.subtitle: Reference Architecture
meta.description: Customers reach a web application through CloudFront with AWS WAF, an Application Load Balancer in public subnets and EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group in private subnets. The application talks to Amazon RDS in isolated subnets and to Secrets Manager and S3 over VPC endpoints; operators administer the instances through Systems Manager Session Manager with no inbound SSH. Adapted from the AWS Architecture Center's web application hosting reference architecture, set at AWS's sample organization AnyCompany.
meta.author: DigitalPrez, LLC
meta.objective: Serve one public web application from private subnets, with every data store and secret reachable only from the application tier and every administrative path brokered by Session Manager.
meta.flow_summary: Customer to the web tier; API to RDS, Secrets Manager and S3; operator to Session Manager
meta.access_summary: Customers: Cognito with MFA (OIDC). Operators: IAM Identity Center with a FIDO2 key and Session Manager. Services: IAM roles, no stored keys.
assumptions: One production account under AWS Organizations with service control policies applied
Two Availability Zones; the Auto Scaling group spans both
Secrets Manager rotates the database password; the application reads it at start
out_of_scope: The CI/CD pipeline that builds AMIs and deploys
The data warehouse that reads RDS snapshots

auth_types.label: Cognito + MFA (OIDC)
auth_types.description: Customer sign-in through an Amazon Cognito user pool with MFA; the application receives OIDC tokens.

auth_types.label: CloudFront Origin Secret Header
auth_types.description: A custom header with a secret value that the ALB listener rule requires; identifies CloudFront as the caller.

auth_types.label: Target Group · No Client Auth
auth_types.description: The load balancer forwards to targets without client authentication; the security group admits only the load balancer.

auth_types.label: IAM Role (SigV4)
auth_types.description: The instance's IAM role signs AWS API calls; no stored keys.

auth_types.label: RDS IAM Authentication + TLS
auth_types.description: Short-lived IAM database tokens over TLS; no database password in the application.

auth_types.label: CloudFront Origin Access Control
auth_types.description: CloudFront signs S3 requests with SigV4; the bucket policy admits only this distribution.

auth_types.label: IAM Identity Center + FIDO2
auth_types.description: Operator sign-in with a security key; permission sets grant time-bound access.

auth_types.label: Session Manager (IAM)
auth_types.description: Sessions authorised by IAM through Identity Center permission sets and logged to CloudWatch; no inbound port.

layers.name: illustrative-threats
layers.label: Illustrative Threats
layers.description: Example threats and controls. Hide to see the plain design.

zones.name: aws-account
zones.label: AWS Account: Production
zones.info: One production account under AWS Organizations; service control policies deny public S3 ACLs, IMDSv1 launches and region use outside us-east-1.

zones.name: vpc-prod
zones.label: Production VPC
zones.info: Three subnet tiers in two Availability Zones. Flow logs go to CloudWatch; GuardDuty analyses them.

appliances.name: nacl-public
appliances.label: NACL
appliances.info: Network ACL on the public subnets: inbound 443 from anywhere, ephemeral ports outbound; everything else denied.

appliances.name: sg-app
appliances.label: SG: App Tier
appliances.info: Security group on the instances: inbound 443 from the ALB security group only; no inbound 22.

appliances.name: sg-db
appliances.label: SG: Database
appliances.info: Security group on the RDS instance: inbound 5432 from the application security group only.

zones.name: aws-services
zones.label: AWS Regional Services
zones.sub: Secrets Manager · S3 · CloudWatch · Systems Manager
zones.info: Regional AWS services the application uses. The VPC reaches them through interface and gateway endpoints, never over the Internet.

appliances.name: vpce
appliances.label: VPC Endpoints
appliances.info: Interface endpoints for Secrets Manager, Systems Manager and CloudWatch, a gateway endpoint for S3; endpoint policies limit the S3 endpoint to buckets in this account.

nodes.name: customer
nodes.label: Customer
nodes.info: A shopper on the public Internet.

nodes.name: cognito
nodes.label: Cognito User Pool
nodes.info: Holds customer identities; advanced security mode scores sign-ins and requires MFA on risk.

nodes.name: cloudfront
nodes.label: CloudFront + AWS WAF
nodes.sub: Edge · TLS 1.2+ · Managed Rules · Rate Limit
nodes.info: The only public entry point. AWS WAF with managed rule groups and a rate-based rule is attached to the distribution.

nodes.name: attacker
nodes.label: Internet Attacker
nodes.info: Opportunistic attacker probing the public surface.

nodes.name: identity-center
nodes.label: IAM Identity Center
nodes.info: Workforce sign-in for operators; permission sets map to IAM roles in the account.

nodes.name: operator
nodes.label: Operations Engineer
nodes.info: Administers instances through Session Manager; never holds long-lived access keys.

nodes.name: alb
nodes.label: Application Load Balancer
nodes.info: Public listener on 443; its security group admits only the CloudFront managed prefix list, and a listener rule requires the origin secret header.

nodes.name: nat
nodes.label: NAT Gateway
nodes.info: Outbound Internet access for the private subnets. Nothing filters what leaves.

nodes.name: web-asg
nodes.label: Web/App Tier
nodes.info: Amazon Linux instances in an Auto Scaling group across two AZs. No public IPs; IMDSv2 required; the SSM agent connects outbound.

components.name: web
components.label: Web Front End
components.info: Serves the storefront; validates Cognito tokens.

components.name: api
components.label: Orders API
components.info: Reads and writes orders; calls RDS, Secrets Manager and S3 with the instance role.

nodes.name: rds
nodes.label: Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL)
nodes.info: Orders and customer records. Not publicly accessible; isolated subnets have no route to the Internet.

nodes.name: s3-assets
nodes.label: S3: Static Assets and Uploads
nodes.info: One bucket for the storefront assets CloudFront serves and the documents customers upload.

nodes.name: secrets
nodes.label: Secrets Manager + KMS
nodes.info: Rotated database credentials and third-party API keys, encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key.

nodes.name: cloudwatch
nodes.label: CloudWatch + CloudTrail
nodes.info: Application and session logs, the organization CloudTrail trail and GuardDuty findings, with alarms to the on-call rotation.

nodes.name: ssm
nodes.label: Systems Manager
nodes.info: Brokers operator sessions to the instances and schedules patching; the agent on each instance connects outbound.

flows.name: f-customer-cognito
flows.label: Sign-In
flows.info: Hosted sign-in with MFA; the browser receives ID and access tokens.

flows.name: f-customer-cf
flows.label: Storefront
flows.info: Every request carries the Cognito access token; TLS terminates at the edge.

flows.name: f-cf-alb
flows.label: Origin Request
flows.info: CloudFront reaches the load balancer over TLS with the origin secret header; the ALB security group admits only the CloudFront prefix list.

flows.name: f-alb-web
flows.label: Forward to Targets
flows.info: Re-encrypted to the instances; the app security group admits only the load balancer.

flows.name: f-web-api
flows.label: Internal Call
flows.info: The front end calls the API on the same instance with the forwarded Cognito token.

flows.name: f-api-rds
flows.label: Orders Database
flows.info: IAM authentication tokens over TLS; the database security group admits only the app tier.

flows.name: f-api-secrets
flows.label: Secrets
flows.info: Reads third-party API keys at start and on rotation through the Secrets Manager interface endpoint.

flows.name: f-api-s3
flows.label: Customer Uploads
flows.info: Uploaded documents go to the bucket through the S3 gateway endpoint; objects are encrypted with the KMS key.

flows.name: f-cf-s3
flows.label: Static Assets (OAC)
flows.info: CloudFront fetches the storefront assets with origin access control; the bucket policy admits only this distribution.

flows.name: f-web-cloudwatch
flows.label: Logs and Metrics
flows.info: The CloudWatch agent ships application logs and metrics through the interface endpoint.

flows.name: f-web-ssm
flows.label: SSM Agent (Outbound)
flows.info: The agent registers with Systems Manager over the interface endpoint; sessions ride this connection, so no inbound port is needed.

flows.name: f-web-nat
flows.label: Outbound via NAT
flows.info: Package updates and any AWS call not covered by an endpoint leave through the NAT gateway. No egress filtering.

flows.name: f-operator-sso
flows.label: Operator Sign-In
flows.info: Identity Center with a FIDO2 key; the permission set grants the operator role for eight hours.

flows.name: f-operator-ssm
flows.label: Session Manager
flows.info: The operator starts a session from the console or CLI; Systems Manager relays it to the agent. Sessions are logged to CloudWatch.

flows.name: f-attacker-cf
flows.label: Credential Stuffing / Scanning
flows.info: Automated traffic hits the only public endpoint; WAF managed rules and the rate-based rule absorb most of it.

flows.name: f-attacker-alb
flows.label: Direct to ALB
flows.blocked_reason: The ALB security group admits only the CloudFront managed prefix list; direct requests never reach a listener

flows.name: f-attacker-s3
flows.label: Public Bucket Access
flows.blocked_reason: Block Public Access at the account level; the bucket policy admits only the CloudFront distribution and the instance role

steps.name: request
steps.title: A customer reaches the application at the edge
steps.description: The customer's browser resolves the storefront name to CloudFront. AWS WAF inspects the request against managed rule groups and a rate-based rule before anything reaches AnyCompany's account; TLS 1.2 or later is required.
details: One public entry point for the whole application
WAF managed rules and rate limiting at the edge

steps.name: edge-origin
steps.title: CloudFront forwards to the load balancer with its origin secret
steps.description: The distribution reaches the Application Load Balancer over TLS. The ALB security group admits only the CloudFront managed prefix list, and a listener rule drops any request without the origin secret header, so the load balancer cannot be reached directly.
details: Security group: CloudFront prefix list only
Listener rule: origin secret header required

steps.name: signin
steps.title: The customer signs in through Cognito
steps.description: Hosted sign-in with MFA issues OIDC tokens; the storefront carries the access token on every request and the web tier validates it against the user pool.
details: MFA enforced; advanced security mode scores sign-ins
Tokens validated by the web tier

steps.name: web-tier
steps.title: The load balancer hands the request to the web tier in private subnets
steps.description: Instances in an Auto Scaling group across two AZs serve the storefront and the Orders API. They have no public IPs; the app security group admits only the load balancer; IMDSv2 is required on every instance.
details: No public IPs, no inbound SSH

steps.name: data
steps.title: The API reaches RDS and Secrets Manager with its instance role
steps.description: IAM authentication tokens open the database connection over TLS; third-party keys come from Secrets Manager through the interface endpoint. No password sits in the application configuration.
details: All of it over private endpoints

steps.name: assets
steps.title: Static assets come from S3 through CloudFront; uploads go to the same bucket
steps.description: CloudFront fetches assets with origin access control; the API writes customer uploads through the S3 gateway endpoint. Block Public Access is on at the account level and the bucket policy names only the distribution and the instance role.
details: Origin access control, no public bucket

steps.name: operate
steps.title: Instances log to CloudWatch and update through the NAT gateway
steps.description: Logs and metrics leave through the CloudWatch interface endpoint; package updates and anything without an endpoint leave through the NAT gateway, which filters nothing.
details: GuardDuty watches flow logs and CloudTrail

steps.name: admin
steps.title: An operator opens a Session Manager session; no inbound port
steps.description: The operator signs in to IAM Identity Center with a FIDO2 key and starts a session from the console. Systems Manager relays it to the agent on the instance over its outbound connection; the session transcript goes to CloudWatch.

steps.name: denied
steps.title: What the attacker cannot do
steps.description: Direct requests to the load balancer and public reads of the bucket are refused before any application code runs; the instances have no public IP and no inbound SSH, and RDS is not publicly accessible, so there is nothing to connect to.
steps.outcome: The public surface is the CloudFront distribution and nothing else.

threats.title: Credential Stuffing and MFA Fatigue Against the Cognito User Pool
threats.description: Password lists from other breaches replayed against hosted sign-in; push-style MFA prompts accepted by tired customers.

attack.scenario: Automated sign-in attempts from rotating IP ranges; successful pairs are resold or used to place fraudulent orders.

risk.rationale: Hosted sign-in is public and lists are cheap; a taken-over account exposes PII and payment references.
risk.consequence: An attacker holds a valid customer session and can read and change that customer's orders.

residual.rationale: MFA with advanced security (CTL-0001) stops matched passwords; the WAF rate-based rule (CTL-0002) throttles the campaign.

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

threats.title: Direct Requests to the Load Balancer Bypass CloudFront and the WAF
threats.description: If the ALB accepted traffic from anywhere, an attacker who found its public name could skip the WAF, the rate limit and the edge TLS policy.

attack.scenario: Certificate transparency logs or DNS history reveal the ALB name; the attacker sends injection payloads to it directly.

risk.rationale: Load balancer names are discoverable; without the gate every WAF rule is moot.
risk.consequence: Injection and brute-force traffic reaches the application unfiltered.

residual.rationale: The security group admits only the CloudFront prefix list (CTL-0003) and the listener requires the origin secret (CTL-0004).

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

threats.title: SSRF from the Orders API Reaches the Instance Metadata Service and Steals Role Credentials
threats.description: The image-import feature fetches URLs the customer supplies. Pointed at 169.254.169.254 on an instance that still allows IMDSv1, it returns the temporary credentials of the instance role.

attack.scenario: A crafted import URL makes the API fetch the metadata endpoint; the response is echoed in an error message.
prerequisites: An instance launched without IMDSv2 enforcement

risk.rationale: SSRF is common in URL-fetching features; role credentials open every service the role can call.
risk.consequence: The attacker calls AWS APIs as the instance role from anywhere.

residual.rationale: IMDSv2 with hop limit 1 (CTL-0005) makes the metadata service unreachable through a forwarded request; AWS Config flags any instance without it.

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

threats.title: Bucket Misconfiguration Exposes Customer Uploads to the Internet
threats.description: A bucket policy or ACL added during a support case could make the uploads prefix readable by anyone, as happened in many published breaches.

attack.scenario: Bucket-name scanners find the bucket within hours of a public grant and copy everything listable.

risk.rationale: Account-level Block Public Access makes the grant impossible rather than merely unlikely.
risk.consequence: Customer documents readable by anyone with the URL.

residual.rationale: Block Public Access is enforced by the account and an SCP; the bucket policy admits only the distribution and the role (CTL-0006).

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

threats.title: Over-Broad Instance Role Reads Every Secret and Opens the Database as Its Master User
threats.description: The instance role carries secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on every secret in the account and the role-based database user is also the master user. Any code running on the instance, legitimate or not, inherits the lot.

attack.scenario: Code running on the instance, through SSRF or a compromised dependency, lists and reads every secret and connects to the database as the master user.

risk.rationale: The permission is one wildcard away from least privilege and every foothold on the instance becomes full data access.
risk.consequence: Any compromise of the web tier is a compromise of the whole data layer.

residual.rationale: GuardDuty and CloudTrail (CTL-0007) see unusual GetSecretValue calls after the fact; nothing prevents them.

projected.rationale: Per-secret resource policies and a least-privilege role (CTL-0008) limit the role to the two secrets it needs and a non-master database user.

suggested_mitigations.text: Replace the role-based database user with a least-privilege application user and keep the master credential in Secrets Manager with no application access.

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

threats.title: Unrestricted Egress Through the NAT Gateway Enables Exfiltration and Command-and-Control
threats.description: The private subnets route all Internet-bound traffic through the NAT gateway with no domain or destination filtering, so a compromised instance can talk to any host and copy data out.

attack.scenario: After a foothold on an instance, query results and documents are posted to an attacker-controlled host over HTTPS; the NAT gateway forwards it like any update download.

risk.rationale: Open egress is the default; it turns every other compromise into a breach.
risk.consequence: Data leaves the account unnoticed until the bill or a GuardDuty finding says so.

residual.rationale: GuardDuty flow-log findings (CTL-0007) can detect known-bad destinations; unknown hosts pass.

projected.rationale: A Network Firewall domain allow-list in front of the NAT gateway (CTL-0009) limits egress to update repositories and approved APIs.

suggested_mitigations.text: Route the private subnets through AWS Network Firewall with a domain allow-list before the NAT gateway, and alarm on denied flows.

provenance.notes: Illustrative example for the reference architecture.

controls.name: Cognito: MFA Required and Advanced Security Mode Enforced
AWS WAF: Managed Rule Groups and a Rate-Based Rule at CloudFront
ALB Security Group Admits Only the CloudFront Managed Prefix List
Listener Rule Requires the CloudFront Origin Secret Header
IMDSv2 Required with Hop Limit 1 on Every Instance
S3 Block Public Access (Account and SCP) with an OAC-Only Bucket Policy
GuardDuty, the Organization CloudTrail Trail and VPC Flow Logs with Alarms
Least-Privilege Instance Role with Per-Secret Resource Policies and a Non-Master Database User
Egress Filtering: Network Firewall Domain Allow-List in Front of the NAT Gateway
Session Manager Only: No Inbound SSH, Sessions Logged to CloudWatch
RDS: Not Publicly Accessible, IAM Authentication, TLS Required, KMS Encryption

attack_paths.title: SSRF to Role Credentials to Database Exfiltration
attack_paths.description: A crafted import URL steals the instance role from the metadata service; the over-broad role reads the database master credentials from Secrets Manager; the database is read from the instance; the results leave through the unfiltered NAT gateway.

hops.note: A crafted image-import URL travels through CloudFront and the load balancer to the API, which fetches 169.254.169.254; on an instance still answering IMDSv1 the role's temporary credentials come back in the error message.

The stolen role is the database's IAM master-equivalent user and may read every secret in the account besides; from the instance, a client dumps the orders tables and the database security group sees an ordinary application connection.
The dump is staged on the instance's disk next to the application; nothing on the host inspects it.
The dump is posted to an attacker-controlled host over HTTPS; the NAT gateway forwards it like any package download.

attack_paths.impact: Customer orders, PII and payment references copied out of the account: regulatory notification, card-brand exposure and a full credential rotation.

risk.rationale: Every hop needs a misconfiguration that AWS Config or GuardDuty would flag, but none of them stops the chain by itself.

residual.rationale: IMDSv2 enforcement (CTL-0005) removes hop 1 on every compliant instance; hops 2 to 4 remain open.

projected.rationale: Per-secret policies (CTL-0008) and egress filtering (CTL-0009) break hops 2 and 4; what is left is the instance itself.
